Compute the Monte Carlo weight $w_k = \Psi(\mathbf{v}_n^{(k)} \mid \mathbf{q}, \omega_o)^{-1} |\mathbf{n} \cdot \omega_i^{(k)}|$ [S1].

The claim states the formula for the Monte Carlo weight $w_k$ as $w_k = Ψ(𝐯_n^{(k)} ∣ 𝐪, ω_o)^{-1} |𝐧 ⋅ ω_i^{(k)}|$. Looking at Source [S1], specifically Algorithm 1 (PathTracePixelDDF), line 13 explicitly defines the weight as: $w_k ← Ψ(𝐯_n^{(k)} ∣ 𝐪, ω_o)^{-1} |𝐧 ⋅ ω_i^{(k)}|$. The variables match exactly: $Ψ$ is the sampling distribution, $𝐯_n^{(k)}$ is the sampled direction, $𝐪$ is the point, $ω_o$ is the outgoing direction, $𝐧$ is the normal, and $ω_i^{(k)}$ is the incoming direction. Therefore, the evidence fully supports the claim.
